heading: INT. LIBRARY INSIDE GIANT TORTOISE SHELL - NIGHT

units.text: INT. LIBRARY INSIDE GIANT TORTOISE SHELL - NIGHT
A cathedral of bone-white arches curving overhead, every rib lined with shelves of crumbling scrolls.
Lanterns hang on slow chains.
The floor sways in a gentle, immense rhythm, as though the whole library were breathing.
ARCHIVIST ELOWEN, thirties, in a gray robe, ink on her fingers, climbs a rolling ladder with a scroll tucked under her arm.
A STRANGER, forties, in a travel-worn cloak, steps through the narrow doorway at the base of the shell.
Snow dusts his shoulders.
He sets down a staff carved with spirals.
Forgive the hour. I seek the book of true names.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: No one seeks it. It finds them.
units.name: ELOWEN

units.text: Then perhaps it has found me.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Perhaps. Your name?
units.name: ELOWEN

units.text: I have not carried one in a long time.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: She descends.
The ladder creaks.
She walks to him and studies his face by lantern light, the scar through his left brow, the grey in his beard.
I know that scar.
units.name: ELOWEN

units.text: I doubt it.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: You were a prince, once. Of the drowned towns.
units.name: ELOWEN

units.text: I was a boy once. A prince is only a boy with a good tailor.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: She reaches for a high shelf and brings down a bound volume, its cover cracked, its clasp rusted.
She opens it, turns three pages, and reads aloud.
"Tamsin, son of the tide. Sworn to forget, and failing."
units.name: ELOWEN

units.text: The Stranger closes his eyes.
The floor lurches, a great slow tremor, as the tortoise stirs beneath them.
Dust falls from the arches.
You have spoken it.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: Tamsin.
units.name: ELOWEN

units.text: Then you know what comes.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: The sea.
units.name: ELOWEN

units.text: He nods.
Far below the floor, something vast begins to move toward the sound of his name.
